claude.sample_unit: pediatric ischaemic stroke patients (full free-text records)

links.outcome: Whether entropy-based uncertainty signals identify misclassified extractions for selective expert review
links.effect: Entropy in misclassified cases was 2.4–3.4 times higher than in correct cases; complete error coverage by reviewing <10% of patients for hemiplegia (8.3%) and headache (8.2%), 19.6% for seizure.
links.quote: Entropy in misclassified cases was 2.4–3.4 times higher than in correctly classified cases.

links.outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and temperatures, measured as entropy across 15 calls
links.effect: Each model-target combination was run 15 times (five temperatures × three repeats); entropy across calls flagged likely errors, with higher entropy in misclassified cases (2.4–3.4 times).
links.quote: Each combination received 15 calls (five temperatures × three repeats).

screen.reason: The study evaluates open LLMs for clinical information extraction and specifically tests an uncertainty-aware triage safeguard (using Shannon entropy across repeated calls to route low-confidence outputs to expert review) to minimize clinician workload while capturing errors.
